extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Specifies the precise technical data and hypotheses (field, curve, prime, coverings, places, cusps, and group-theoretic conditions) that constitute 'initial Θ-data' used to build Θ-Hodge theaters and to carry out subsequent constructions in IUT; also records several auxiliary technical definitions/corrections (Galois-countability, coherence, strengthened conditions (cnew),(dnew), and discrete/profinite group properties).

rubrics_metrics.name: T1: Galois-countable (tempered groups/temperoids/quasi-temperoids)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall say that a tempered group is Galois-countable if its topology admits a countable basis. We shall say that a connected temperoid is Galois-countable if it arises from a Galois-countable tempered group. We shall say that a temperoid is Galois-countable if it arises from a collection of Galois-countable connected temperoids. We shall say that a connected quasi-temperoid is Galois-countable if it arises from a Galois-countable connected temperoid. We shall say that a quasi-temperoid is Galois-countable if it arises from a collection of Galois-countable connected quasi-temperoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces a countability hypothesis necessary to avoid pathologies in the theory of tempered fundamental groups; used to ensure existence of compatible basepoints for universal covering pro-objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: T2: Galois-countable semi-graph of anabelioids
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall say that a semi-graph of anabelioids G is Galois-countable if it is countable, and, moreover, admits a countable collection of finite étale coverings {Gi → G}i∈I such that for any finite étale covering H → G, there exists an i ∈ I such that the base-changed covering H ×G Gi → Gi splits over the constituent anabelioid associated to each component of [the underlying semi-graph of] Gi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concrete countability condition on semi-graphs ensuring the splitting behavior of coverings; used to make tempered fundamental group constructions well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: T3: strictly coherent semi-graph of anabelioids
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall say that a semi-graph of anabelioids G is strictly coherent if it is coherent and, moreover, each of the profinite groups associated to components c of G is topologically generated by N generators, for some positive integer N independent of c. In particular, if G is finite and coherent then it is strictly coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strengthening of coherence that uniformly bounds minimal topological generator numbers across components; implies Galois-countability when combined with countability.

rubrics_metrics.name: T4: consequence of strict coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: One verifies immediately that every strictly coherent, countable semi-graph of anabelioids is Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logical consequence: strict coherence + countability ⇒ T2 holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: T5: countability implies tempered fundamental group well-defined
rubrics_metrics.description: If the temperoid X is Galois-countable then its associated tempered fundamental group πtemp(X) is well-defined and Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures tempered fundamental group may be defined intrinsically (existence of compatible basepoints).

rubrics_metrics.name: T6: countability for semi-graphs implies πtemp(G) and Btemp(G) well-defined
rubrics_metrics.description: If the semi-graph of anabelioids G is Galois-countable, then its associated tempered fundamental group πtemp(G) and temperoid Btemp(G) are well-defined and Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous statement to (T5) in the semi-graph context.

rubrics_metrics.name: E1: topological subquotients of absolute Galois groups are Galois-countable
rubrics_metrics.description: All topological subquotients of absolute Galois groups of fields of countable cardinality are Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show that many naturally occurring tempered groups satisfy countability hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: E2: tamely ramified arithmetic fundamental groups are Galois-countable
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is a field whose absolute Galois group is Galois-countable, and U is a nonempty open subscheme of a connected proper k-scheme X that arises as the underlying scheme of a log scheme that is log smooth over k (with Spec(k) the trivial log structure) and whose interior is equal to U, then the tamely ramified arithmetic fundamental group of U is itself Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to common arithmetic situations (tamely ramified coverings) to guarantee countability.

rubrics_metrics.name: E3: examples in SemiAnbd are Galois-countable / strictly coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempered groups and temperoids in [SemiAnbd] Examples 2.10, 3.10, and 5.6 are Galois-countable, while the semi-graphs of anabelioids appearing in those examples are strictly coherent and hence Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the countability fixes do not affect those examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: E4: no effect on SemiAnbd §6
rubrics_metrics.description: It follows immediately from (E3) that there is no effect on [SemiAnbd], §6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-note on propagation of countability assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: E5: no effect on SemiAnbd §4 and §5 under strengthened hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: It follows from items (T3), (T4), together with finiteness and coherence assumptions and the assumption of coherence in [SemiAnbd], Deﬁnition 5.1, (i), (d), that there is no effect on [SemiAnbd], §4, §5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which portions of [SemiAnbd] require added countability assumptions and that these are harmless under given hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: E6: no effect on SemiAnbd §1, §2, Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no effect on [SemiAnbd], §1, §2, or the Appendix of [SemiAnbd], since tempered fundamental groups are never discussed in these portions of [SemiAnbd].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta observation separating portions affected by countability.

rubrics_metrics.name: E7: require Galois-countability in numbered results of SemiAnbd
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Deﬁnitions/Propositions/Theorems/Corollaries of [SemiAnbd] numbered 3.2–3.9, one must assume that all tempered groups, temperoids, and semi-graphs of anabelioids that appear are Galois-countable. However, (E1),(E2),(E3) imply no effect on remaining portions of §3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies where the additional hypothesis must be inserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: E8: require Galois-countability in QuCnf and FrdII
rubrics_metrics.description: In [QuCnf] and [FrdII], one must assume that all tempered groups and [quasi-]temperoids that appear are Galois-countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propagation of the countability correction to other papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: E9: no effect beyond SemiAnbd and cited papers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no effect on any papers of the author other than [SemiAnbd] and the papers discussed in (E8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bounding the scope of the necessary corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction (iii): determination of edge and boundary morphisms from vertex morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism classes of the φv completely determine the isomorphism class of each of the φe, as well as each isomorphism φb, up to composition with an automorphism of the composite 1-morphism of anabelioids Ge → Hf → Hw that arises from an automorphism of the 1-morphism Ge → Hf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces an incorrect assertion in [SemiAnbd]; adds the caveat that determination is up to composition by certain automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural requirement: every edge abuts at least one vertex
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to assume further that the semi-graphs of anabelioids that appear satisfy the condition that every edge abuts to at least one vertex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional combinatorial condition needed where the original exposition omitted it.

rubrics_metrics.name: O1: existence of cofinal countable collection of characteristic finite étale Galois coverings (G finite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose that G is finite. Then G admits a cofinal, countable collection of connected finite étale Galois coverings {Gi → G}i∈I, each of which is characteristic (i.e., any pull-back of the covering via an element of Aut(G) is isomorphic to the original covering). For instance, such a collection may be obtained by considering, for n positive integer, the composite of all connected finite étale Galois coverings of degree ≤ n. We may assume this collection arises from a projective system (G^{•}). Thus one obtains a natural exact sequence 1 → Gal(G^{•}/G) → Aut(G^{•}/G) → Aut(G) → 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to equip Aut(G[c]) with a natural profinite topology; underlies (O2) and the definitions of (cnew) and (dnew).

rubrics_metrics.name: O2: profinite topology on Aut(G) via finite index normal subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: For i∈I consider finite index normal subgroup Aut_i(G^{•}/G) ⊆ Aut(G^{•}/G) inducing identity on underlying semi-graph Gi and on Gal(Gi/G). The intersection of Aut_i(G^{•}/G) is {1}; these Aut_i determine a natural profinite topology on Aut(G^{•}/G) and hence on Aut(G), compatible with profinite topology on Gal(G^{•}/G) and independent of choice of G^{•}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs the topology used to state continuity in (cnew).

rubrics_metrics.name: cnew: strengthened condition on H-action continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of H on G is trivial; the resulting homomorphism H → Aut(G[c]), where c ranges over components (vertices and edges) of G, is continuous (i.e., relative to the natural profinite group topology defined in (O2) on Aut(G[c])).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger version of condition (c) in [SemiAnbd], Deﬁnition 5.1, (i); implies (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: dnew: strengthened finiteness/uniformity condition for components
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a finite set C* of components (vertices and edges) of G such that for every component c of G, there exists c* ∈ C* and an isomorphism of semi-graphs of anabelioids G[c] ∼→ G[c*] that is compatible with the action of H on both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger version of condition (d) in [SemiAnbd], Deﬁnition 5.1, (i); implies (d) and is needed to lift H-actions compatibly over edges in coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: O3: openness of finite-index subgroups of H (topologically finitely generated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since H is topologically finitely generated, it holds that every finite index subgroup of H is open in H. Thus the conditions (c) and (cnew) in fact hold automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation that makes (cnew) and (c) automatically satisfied in the intended context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.6: profinite conjugates of discrete subgroups (statement and conclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a group containing finite index subgroup G ⊆ F with G either free discrete of finite rank or orientable surface group; H ⊆ F an infinite subgroup. Write closures in profinite completion. Let γ ∈ (profinite F) be such that γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ F (equivalently H ⊆ γ^{-1}·F·γ). Then γ ∈ F · N_{(profinite F)}(  ar{H G} ), i.e., γ· ar{H G}·γ^{-1} = δ· ar{H G}·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ F. If moreover  ar{H G} is nonabelian then γ ∈ F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a criterion describing when an element of the profinite completion that conjugates an infinite subgroup back into the discrete group must already lie (up to normalizer) in the discrete group; proof uses conjugacy separability and structural lemmas about free/surface groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(i): two-generator subgroups are free
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subgroup of G generated by two elements of G is free (if G is free; for orientable surface groups follows from Johansson-type result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard fact used repeatedly in the proofs; supports (iii),(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(ii): existence of finite-index subgroup making element visible in abelianization
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x ∈ G be nontrivial. Then there exists a finite index subgroup G1 ⊆ G such that x ∈ G1 and x has nontrivial image in the abelianization Gab1 of G1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to separate elements in finite quotients and to ensure torsion-freeness in abelianizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(iii): produce rank-two free abelian image from noncommuting elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x,y ∈ G be noncommuting. Then there exists finite index G1 ⊆ G and positive integer n such that x^n,y^n ∈ G1 and the images of x^n,y^n in Gab1 generate a free abelian subgroup of rank two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key to distinguishing nonabelian behavior in abelianizations after passing to finite index subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(iv): abelian subgroups are cyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: Any abelian subgroup of G is cyclic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard structural property of free groups and surface groups; used in classification of subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(v): closed subgroup surjecting to pro-Z is normally terminal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T̄ ⊆ Ĝ be a closed subgroup with a continuous surjection Ĝ → Ẑ inducing an isomorphism T̄ → Ẑ. Then T̄ is normally terminal in Ĝ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A profinite cohomological argument yields normal terminality; used to control normalizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(vi): centralizer of kernel of profinite→abelianization is trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N̂ be kernel of natural surjection Ĝ → Ĝ^{ab}. Then the centralizer Z_{Ĝ}(N̂) is trivial (when G nonabelian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce rigidity of automorphisms and centralizers in profinite completions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.7(vii): automorphism trivial if fixes kernel N̂ pointwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Let α be an automorphism of profinite group Ĝ that preserves and restricts to the identity on N̂. Then α is the identity automorphism of Ĝ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concludes automorphisms are trivial under strong fixed-kernel hypotheses; used to control outer automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2.8: profinite conjugates in topological fundamental groups of complex hyperbolic curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Z be a hyperbolic curve over C. Write ΠZ for topological fundamental group and its profinite completion. Let H ⊆ ΠZ be infinite and γ ∈ profinite ΠZ with γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ ΠZ. Then γ ∈ ΠZ · N_{profinite}(  ar{H} ). If H is nonabelian then γ ∈ ΠZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Theorem 2.6 to topological fundamental groups; useful specifically when H is a cuspidal inertia group in the non-proper case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(a): field and basic notation for initial Θ-data
rubrics_metrics.description: F is a number field such that (text formatting): Write GF def= Gal(F/F). -1 ∈ F; F is an algebraic closure of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up base field notation and the presence of the involution −1 used later; precise formatting in original may be slightly garbled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(b): XF once-punctured elliptic curve with stable reduction and associated notation
rubrics_metrics.description: XF is a once-punctured elliptic curve (a hyperbolic curve of type (1,1)) over F that admits stable reduction over all v ∈ V(F)non. Write EF for the elliptic curve over F determined by XF (so XF ⊆ EF). XF → CF for the hyperbolic orbicurve over F obtained by forming the stack-theoretic quotient of XF by the unique F-involution '−1' of XF; Fmod ⊆ F for the field of moduli of XF; Fsol ⊆ F for the maximal solvable extension of Fmod in F; Vmod def= V(Fmod). Then Vbad_mod ⊆ Vmod is a nonempty set of nonarchimedean valuations of Fmod of odd residue characteristic such that XF has bad (i.e., multiplicative) reduction at elements of V(F) lying over Vbad_mod. Write Vgood_mod def= Vmod \ Vbad_mod. Various π1 and Π groups Δ(−), Π(−) are introduced with natural exact sequences 1 → Δ(−) → Π(−)_F → G_F → 1. Assume F/Fmod is Galois of degree prime to l, and the 2·3-torsion points of EF are rational over F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies geometry and Galois hypotheses on the elliptic curve/orbicurve used in the Θ-data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(c): prime l and Galois image condition
rubrics_metrics.description: l is a prime ≥ 5 such that the image of the outer homomorphism G_F → GL2(F_l) determined by the l-torsion points of E_F contains SL2(F_l); write K ⊆ F for the finite Galois extension of F determined by the kernel. Also assume l is prime to residue characteristics in Vbad_mod and prime to orders of q-parameters (local heights) of E_F at primes of V(F)bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong irreducibility/large image condition on l-torsion; used to produce the (1,l-tors) type orbicurves and control ramifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(d): C^K hyperbolic orbicurve and associated coverings X^K, compatibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: C^K is a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1,l-tors)^{±} over K, with K-core C_K def= C_F ×_F K. C^K determines up to K-isomorphism a hyperbolic orbicurve X^K of type (1,l-tors) over K together with natural cartesian diagrams of finite étale coverings and corresponding open immersions of profinite groups Π_{X^K} → Π_{C^K} → Π_{X_F} → Π_{C_F} and analogous Δ inclusions. By [EtTh] Proposition 2.2, Δ_C admits uniquely determined open subgroups Δ_X ⊆ Δ_C ⊆ Δ_C corresponding to finite étale coverings of specified types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the existence and compatibility of certain finite étale coverings and associated group inclusions that are part of the Θ-data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(e): choice of places V ⊆ V(K) and local models
rubrics_metrics.description: V ⊆ V(K) induces a natural bijection V → Vmod (i.e., a section of the natural surjection V(K) → Vmod). Write Vnon, Vbad, Vgood, Varc, etc., for decompositions. For each v ∈ V(K) use subscript v for base-change to K_v; obtain cartesian diagrams of proﬁnite étale coverings and injections of profinite étale fundamental groups. The decomposition group G_v ⊆ G_K is determined up to G_K-conjugacy by v. If v ∈ Vbad then C_v is of type (1,Z/lZ)^{±}, and by 'extracting an l-th root of the theta function' X_v and C_v admit natural models over K_v which are hyperbolic orbicurves of types (1,(Z/lZ)Θ) etc.; these models determine open subgroups Π_{X_v} ⊆ Π_{C_v}. For v ∈ Vgood we write Π_v def= Π^{tp}_{X_v}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies local base-change behavior and the existence of local models in the bad reduction cases with l-root extractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1(f): distinguished cusp c^K and its local incarnations
rubrics_metrics.description: c^K is a cusp of the hyperbolic orbicurve C^K arising from a nonzero element of the quotient 'Q' in the definition of hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1,l-tors)^{±}. For v ∈ V write c^K_v for the cusp of C_v determined by c^K. If v ∈ Vbad assume c^K_v is the cusp arising from the canonical generator (±1) of the quotient Z in the definition of hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1,Z/lZ)^{±}. Thus the data (X^K, C^K, c^K) determine hyperbolic orbicurves X^{−→K}, C^{−→K} and corresponding open subgroups Π_{X^{−→v}} ⊆ Π_{C^{−→v}}; if v ∈ Vgood write Π_{X^{−→v}} def= Π_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixes a distinguished cusp compatible with the orbicurve types; used to control inertia/cuspidal groups in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 3.1.1: tempered fundamental groups and dependence on v
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative to the notation of Definition 3.1(e), suppose v ∈ Vnon. Then in addition to profinite groups Π(−)_v, Δ(−) one also has corresponding tempered fundamental groups Π^{tp}(−)_v, Δ^{tp}(−)_v whose profinite completions may be identified with Π(−)_v, Δ(−). Note that unlike Δ(−), the topological group Δ^{tp}(−)_v depends, a priori, on v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how tempered groups arise locally and warns of v-dependence of topological tempered groups even when profinite completions are canonical.
